terminal.emulator: direct PTY with probe-owned delayed loopback HTTP/SSE server

reference.capture: fresh Hades debug processes with explicit loopback provider configuration and separated response writes

normalization: The binary path, synthetic HOME/HERMES_HOME, PTY path, timestamps, session identifiers, prompt contents, and raw ANSI redraw stream are omitted or replaced by stable markers.

The provider binds only to 127.0.0.1 and records method/path, content type, authorization presence, body keys, model, stream flag, message roles, and tool presence; no API key is configured or persisted.

The server releases the second SSE delta only after the replay observes the first delta, and in the cancellation case releases it only after Ctrl+C; this proves ordering without claiming a universal time constant.
Connection closure is represented by a server-side write failure after cancellation; kernel buffering may allow a late write attempt before the close is detected.

steps.precondition: Fresh Hades 120x40 PTY with HADES_PROVIDER_BASE_URL set to a probe-owned loopback endpoint. The server writes HADES_DELAY_FIRST, waits for the replay assertion, then writes HADES_DELAY_SECOND, finish, and DONE.

Fresh Hades 120x40 PTY with the same loopback server. After HADES_DELAY_FIRST is visible, Ctrl+C is sent before HADES_DELAY_SECOND is released; the replay then releases the second write to test the closed connection boundary.

unknowns: This proves a bounded loopback ordering and cancellation boundary only; no universal redraw latency, timeout, or maximum token claim is made.
A provider write may succeed from kernel buffering after cancellation before the server observes the closed socket; exact byte-level cutoff remains timing-sensitive.

Hades retries, subsequent chat requests, tool execution, malformed/error response presentation, non-loopback providers, HTTPS, credentials, OAuth, persistence, and model discovery remain outside this replay.
